title: Alacritty process hang on close
body:
I noticed that when I close Alacritty, through an exit for example, the window closes normally, but the shortcut icon progress bar keeps spinning and I am unable to open another instance till it stops, and even a bit more after it stops, only after.

I am using this ppa https://launchpad.net/~aslatter/+archive/ubuntu/ppa with the latest version, even though when installing it says `0.13.1`, when I do a `-v`, it shows `0.14.0-dev`.

I use nushell, zellij and starship with it.

PopOS 22.04

Laptop with very good hardware. Certainly not the problem.

I was using Terminator as the terminal before and never had this kind of behavior, not a really bad thing, but sometimes it could be, that's why I opened the issue.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
What makes you think Alacritty isn't closing? When opening Alacritty from a terminal, does it not return to the prompt immediately?

This sounds like it's just a DE issue tbh.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I just described why, but will do again, there is that spinning (loading indicator) that keeps rotating on the shortcut, indicating that the process has not yet closed (even though the window has closed), and also a bit after the spin is gone, I am still not able to open another Alacritty instance. It does nothing If I click on it to open. That is why.

comments.body: Do you see alacritty in the process tree?


However alacritty doesn't try to connect to any running instance, it should create new when you run it again, thus it's likely an issue with DE or driver.

It does nothing If I click on it to open. That is why.

I believe I am experiencing the same issue. When I launch Alacritty through a terminal command, it functions as expected: I can open, close, and instantly reopen it without any problems. However, attempting to initiate Alacritty using a shortcut or by clicking its icon leads to a persistent spinning cursor, which remains even after closing Alacritty. Moreover, I'm unable to relaunch it (either via shortcut or icon) for a brief period, about 7 to 8 seconds.

Based on what I've read in other issues here and after testing both Alacritty versions 0.13.1 and 0.14.0 (with and without the suggested patch), my understanding is that the problem might be related to GNOME itself. I was hopeful that the new GNOME version 45.4 would address this, but unfortunately, it has not. I genuinely miss using Alacritty.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I suppose a solution was provided.

Find the `.desktop` config, usually at `/usr/share/applications/com.alacritty.Alacritty.desktop` and change `StartupNotify` to `false`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
It doesn't make any sense that `StartupNotify` will affect close.

I do understand _start_, but close? There was also a bug with startup notify, which master _fixed_, but not sure if it's related.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I confirm that setting `StartupNotify` to `false` solves the problem for me.

AFAICT it indeed affects **start**, not close, but it's easy to think it affects close because at least I first noticed the issue when starting Alacritty, closing it right away and then trying to start it again. The spinning mouse cursor shows up for me immediately after *starting* Alacritty and stays around for roughly 10 seconds even after closing Alacritty, that is even when I see Alacritty disappearing from the process tree. I guess when the user just starts Alacritty, maximizes the window and goes about his/her business it's easy to miss the fact that hovering the Gnome dock shows a spinning cursor that's gone after some seconds.

BTW, I'm pretty sure I've observed the same behavior with Google Chrome so there is a very good chance this isn't an Alacritty bug. But I have no idea why these two specific apps show this behavior while others don't.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The log looks _cut_(start of it) and it seems that the startup notify token is not passed based on that to the application at all, while it should. You can test with `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN="token" alacritty -vv` and see the `token: "token"` somewhere in the log, that's what `StartupNotify` should do, since gnome sets the token and we just load it.

I'm not sure which gnome version you have, could be just a gnome bug, since on fedora everything is fine and gnome properly activates alacritty.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
That's the entire log file. New log files written by Alacritty also have the same format for me.

My Gnome version is `42.9`.

In any case, I have a very functional workaround and don't see a need to spend more time on this if I'm the only one with this problem.

Thanks a lot for your help (and for maintaining a superb terminal emulator).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Oh, that gnome version could explain that, since it's likely doesn't have startup notify for wayland at all in it, thus it just breaks for you since it expects some kind of startup notify, but it's not even present in it, probably wants some kind of dbus or x11 startup notify.

So your option would be to only wait for gnome to update (the current is 47), since it was _gnome bug_ that got fixed.
